title: Blessed Is the One Who Comes
hookLine: blessings and visits greet a new baby
carry: a new life is greeted with a blessing

lines: THEY BLESS, AND THEY NAME HIM.
cards: Bethlehem, at the end of the book of Ruth. A baby boy has just been born to Ruth and Boaz. The scene the book chooses to show isn't the birth.
It's the neighbors. The women of the town crowd around Naomi, the grandmother, the one who came home bitter and empty-handed. They bless God for her.
They tell her this child will restore her life and care for her when she's old. Naomi takes the baby and holds him to her chest. Then the women do one more thing: they give him his name, Obed.
A child arrives, and the street shows up.

teach.b: First, a blessing for good news. The Talmud teaches that on hearing good news that brings good to others as well as to you, you bless God as the one who is good and does good.
Some authorities apply it to the birth of a child, a joy the whole household shares. Before the baby has done anything, the first response is gratitude. Second, the visit.
In Ashkenazi custom, on the first Friday night after a boy is born, friends come to the family's home for a gathering called shalom zachar, welcome to the male: snacks, songs, words of Torah.
Sephardi and other communities have their own customs, and families welcome girls with gatherings too, which you'll meet later this week. Nobody greets a new life alone. Third, the words at the door.

teach.h: BLESSED IS THE ONE WHO COMES.
teach.b: When a baby is carried in to a ceremony, people often call out baruch haba, blessed is the one who comes. It echoes a line from the Psalms: "Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the LORD." Fourth, back to Bethlehem.
The women in Ruth don't just congratulate.
They speak about the baby's future and about Naomi's healing.

teach.h: BLESSED IS THE ONE WHO COMES.
teach.b: Welcome, in that story, is a promise: we see this child, and we see the family around him.

how: When a Jewish baby is born, families often recite a blessing of thanks, and in many communities friends gather at the home, such as at a shalom zachar, an Ashkenazi custom on the first Friday night after a boy's birth.

games.q: you're one of the women of Bethlehem. Naomi, who came home bitter, now holds her new grandson. what do you do?
o: leave the family in peace and stay away.
bless God for her and speak of the child's future.
remind her of everything she lost.
games.why: they bless God, tell Naomi the child will restore her life, and even give him his name, Obed.

practice: Bring to mind a baby you know, or have heard about, or one due soon; if none comes to mind, any newcomer will do: a new neighbor, a new coworker, a new pet.

Picture their face, or just their name, and say inside the Psalm's words: blessed is the one who comes. Then add one good thing you hope for them, a hope rather than advice, and if you pray, hold them in your prayer.

wordCard.voice: Welcome. The blessing for good news, the friends who come to the house, and baruch haba at the door. Today's word.
